title: How to Calculate FBR POS Integration Cost
metaDescription: What FBR POS integration really costs in Pakistan — software subscriptions, setup, optional hardware, and hidden costs — and why it is far cheaper than a single penalty.
content:
What FBR POS integration costs

FBR POS integration cost is what a business pays to connect its point of sale to FBR IRIS so every sale is reported in real time with a QR-coded invoice. For most Pakistani businesses this lands in the region of PKR 1,500 to 5,000 per month for a cloud-based system, sometimes with a small setup fee — far less than owners often fear, and a fraction of what a single penalty costs. The real question is not "how much is it?" but "how does it compare to the cost of not doing it?" — and on that comparison, integration is one of the cheapest forms of insurance a business can buy.

This guide breaks down what actually drives the price, the ranges to expect, the hidden costs to watch, and why the numbers almost always favour getting compliant.

What drives the price

A few factors move the cost up or down:

  • Number of branches and terminals — more points of sale means more to register and license.
  • Cloud versus desktop — cloud is subscription-based; desktop is often one-time but shifts update costs to you.
  • Features — inventory, multi-branch reporting, and integrations add value and sometimes cost.
  • Support level — responsive support for token and sync issues may sit in a higher tier.
  • Hardware — usually minimal, since a compliant POS runs on devices you already own.

Typical price ranges

As a rough guide, cloud FBR POS plans commonly run between PKR 1,500 and 5,000 per month, scaling with branches and features, plus an occasional one-time setup fee. Single-outlet businesses sit at the lower end; multi-branch chains pay more for centralised reporting. Providers price differently, so use these as a starting point and get current quotes before deciding.

Cost components at a glance

ComponentTypical treatmentNotes
SoftwareMonthly subscriptionIncludes FBR updates on cloud
Setup / integrationOne-time (often modest)IRIS registration, tax mapping
HardwareOptionalRuns on existing devices
SupportIncluded or tieredMatters for token/sync fixes

Cloud versus desktop, cost-wise

A one-time desktop licence can look cheaper on day one, but it moves the burden of staying compliant onto you: when FBR changes a rule or the IRIS API evolves, you have to update, and many businesses do not. A cloud subscription folds those updates into the monthly fee, so a rule change applies automatically. For most owners the small ongoing cost is worth avoiding the risk of a stale system quietly falling out of compliance — see our fuller comparison of cloud versus desktop FBR POS.

How to budget in five steps

  1. Count your points of sale — branches and terminals drive licensing.
  2. Decide cloud or desktop — factor in who bears update costs.
  3. List must-have features — inventory, multi-branch reporting, support level.
  4. Get itemised quotes — separate software, setup, and any per-terminal fees.
  5. Compare against penalty risk — weigh the annual cost against a single fine.

The comparison that matters

Set the cost beside the alternative. Non-compliance penalties start around PKR 10,000 and can climb to PKR 1,000,000 for repeat violations, with possible STRN suspension on top. Even a higher-end plan at PKR 5,000 per month is PKR 60,000 a year — less than a single serious penalty, and it also saves accountant time on monthly filing. Framed that way, integration is not a cost centre; it is risk reduction that often pays for itself.

A real example

A retailer in Multan hesitated over a PKR 2,500 monthly plan, treating it as an expense to avoid. Two months of delay ended with a compliance check and a penalty well past PKR 100,000 for the unreported period — roughly three years of the subscription they had been avoiding. After integrating, they also found monthly sales-tax filing dropped from days to a short review, quietly offsetting much of the fee.

Spend a little, avoid a lot

For nearly every business, FBR POS integration is far cheaper than the penalties it prevents, and cheaper still once you count the time saved on filing. Confirm you actually need it by checking whether you are a Tier-1 retailer, then keep the setup penalty-free with the FBR compliance checklist. One technical reminder that affects value: a good system refreshes its IRIS token automatically — those tokens expire roughly hourly — so you are paying for reliability, not just software.

faqs.question: How much does FBR POS integration cost in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: Most cloud-based FBR POS systems fall in the range of roughly PKR 1,500 to 5,000 per month depending on branches, terminals, and features, often with a modest one-time setup fee. Prices vary by provider, so treat these as a guide and confirm current quotes.

faqs.question: Do I need to buy expensive hardware?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A compliant POS runs on an Android phone, tablet, or laptop you likely already own. A thermal printer is optional for paper receipts, but QR invoices can also be sent by WhatsApp or SMS, so hardware is rarely a major cost.

faqs.question: Is a one-time or monthly plan better?
faqs.answer: For most businesses a monthly cloud plan is better value because it includes the ongoing FBR rule updates that keep you compliant. A one-time desktop purchase can look cheaper but shifts the cost and risk of staying updated onto you.

faqs.question: Are there hidden costs to watch for?
faqs.answer: Watch for per-branch or per-terminal fees, charges for support, and the cost of updates on one-time software. The biggest hidden cost, though, is non-compliance: a single penalty can exceed a year of subscription fees.

faqs.question: How does the cost compare to the penalties?
faqs.answer: It is far smaller. Non-compliance penalties start around PKR 10,000 and can reach PKR 1,000,000 for repeat offences. Even the higher-end monthly plans cost a fraction of a single first-offence fine.
